items.t: Pledged to uphold the rule of law and support law enforcement as attorney general.
items.q: pledging to uphold the rule of law, support law enforcement and serve the people of Ohio with integrity and transparency.

items.t: Said his office will hold contractors accountable when they take consumers' money and run.
items.q: “Ohioans who pay for home improvements deserve to get the work they paid for,” said Wilson. “We will hold contractors accountable when they take consumers’ money and run.”

record.office: Director of Ohio Department of Public Safety
record.t: Was appointed Director of the Ohio Department of Public Safety by Governor DeWine in December 2022.
record.q: In December of 2022, Governor DeWine appointed Wilson Director of the Ohio Department of Public Safety.

record.t: Served as Governor Mike DeWine's senior advisor for criminal justice policy beginning in January 2019.
record.q: Wilson served as Governor Mike DeWine’s senior advisor for criminal justice policy beginning in January of 2019.

record.t: Was appointed Clark County prosecutor in January 2011.
record.q: In January 2011, he was appointed Clark County prosecutor, overseeing many major criminal cases and developing several innovative programs.

record.t: Started his legal career in 2002 as a trial prosecutor in Clark County.
record.q: Attorney General Wilson started his legal career in 2002 as a trial prosecutor in Clark County, specializing in cases involving sexual and/or physical violence against children.

record.t: Was later elected Clark County prosecutor for two subsequent terms.
record.q: In January of 2011, Wilson was appointed to serve as the Clark County prosecutor and was later elected to that position for two subsequent terms.

record.office: Director, Ohio Department of Public Safety
record.t: Served as director of the Ohio Department of Public Safety before becoming attorney general.
record.q: Before being named Ohio’s 52nd attorney general by Gov. Mike DeWine, he directed the Ohio Department of Public Safety, overseeing the department’s 10 divisions, nearly 4,000 employees, and $2.5 billion biannual budget.

record.office: Director, Ohio Department of Public Safety
record.t: Was named Ohio Attorney General by Governor Mike DeWine to serve the remainder of Dave Yost's term.
record.q: Wilson, who currently serves as the director of the Ohio Department of Public Safety , will serve the remainder of Yost's term

record.t: Began serving as Ohio's 52nd attorney general.
record.q: Andy Wilson began serving as Ohio’s 52nd attorney general today

record.t: Filed a lawsuit in Hamilton County Common Pleas Court against Quincy Barrett and Crown Pointe Remodeling over home improvement services.
record.q: Wilson’s lawsuit , filed in Hamilton County Common Pleas Court, alleges that Cincinnati-based Quincy Barrett and his company, Crown Pointe Remodeling, solicited consumers online and sold home improvement services

record.t: Filed separate lawsuits against two Ohio home-improvement companies over alleged unperformed or subpar work.
record.q: Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson has filed separate lawsuits against two Ohio home-improvement companies that allegedly took down payments from consumers but failed to provide the services promised or performed subpar work.

record.t: Announced, with Belmont County Prosecutor Kevin Flanagan, a guilty verdict for aggravated murder in the 2021 killings of a Belmont County couple.
record.q: An Oklahoma man was found guilty today of aggravated murder in the 2021 killings of a Belmont County couple, Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson and Belmont County Prosecutor Kevin Flanagan announced.

record.t: Announced a nine-year prison sentence for a Cleveland-area man convicted of stealing merchandise from farm-supply stores in 10 counties.
record.q: A Cleveland-area man was sentenced today to nine years in prison for stealing more than $100,000 in merchandise from farm-supply stores in 10 counties, Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson announced.

record.t: Challenged Ohioans and law enforcement agencies statewide to document 250 acts of kindness.
record.q: Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson is challenging Ohioans and law enforcement agencies statewide to join us in documenting 250 acts of kindness.
